summary.headline: Capillary Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR256 crore and adjusted EBITDA to INR44 crore (~17%), with organic growth at 17%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR256 crore, up 43% YoY, with two months of SessionM (acquired May 1, 2026) contributing; organic growth was 17% and currency added about 6%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR44 crore (about 17-18% margin) versus INR19 crore a year earlier, and reported PAT was -INR9.5 crore, or INR25 crore normalised after excluding a cyber-fraud loss and a one-time deferred tax charge. ARR reached INR1,026 crore (+34% YoY), and trailing-12-month new ACV excluding one large healthcare win was about INR92 crore (+75%). Management kept FY27 guidance of INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA unchanged, saying it expects to beat both.

financial_highlights.change: +132% YoY; from INR19 crore; organic EBITDA margin ~23%
Includes cyber-fraud exceptional loss and one-time deferred tax liability
Up from INR19 crore in Q4 FY26
+34% YoY; from INR765 crore in FY26 and INR608 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Trailing-12-month new ACV (ex one healthcare win)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Loyalty stack
segments.commentary: Over 90% of revenue; core product and the business's main monetisation layer. Contracts are typically 3-7 year subscriptions.

segments.name: Engage (Engage+)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; one-to-one personalised customer communication platform.

segments.name: Rewards
segments.commentary: About 5-7% of revenue; mainly banks and telcos.

segments.name: aiRA (AI analytics and action agents)
segments.commentary: About USD2.5 million ARR (~26 customers live, under 10 paying); management targets 5-10% of revenue from aiRA in FY27. Gross margin above 80%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged at INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA; management expects to beat both but did not quantify.
Organic growth expected at about 17% for FY27 (about 20-23% including FX and inorganic); management described 15-20% as the organic run-rate.
Kognitiv: first customer migration to go live September 1, 2026; ~16-17 customers in total; migration of the full base targeted by September 2027, with ~INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift from Kognitiv.

SessionM: management expects EBITDA margin to move from break-even to ~15% within a year and to 35-40% over a further year; server cost savings of USD6-8 million over 3-4 quarters, with a payback possibly within FY27.
ESOP expense guided at INR12-15 crore for FY27, kept at 1-2% of revenue.
New ACV expected to grow at least 30-40% YoY in FY27 (not the 75% trailing figure).
capex_capacity: SessionM acquired from Mastercard effective May 1, 2026; enterprise value USD20 million, net cost about INR17 crore after net-debt true-up on April 30; entities debt-free; SessionM ARR about USD32 million, all contracts agreed to move to Capillary paper.
Kognitiv (closed May 1, 2025): ~16-17 customers; AI-led migration tool; first customer live Sept 1, 2026.
Migration of SessionM customers not expected to start until end-2026 / early 2027; 3-4 of ~45 SessionM customers are being fast-tracked.
Cloud-native platform across four colos; product uptime of nearly 5 nines in Q1.
CustomerGlu tuck-in (rebranded Experiences+) bought for less than a few hundred thousand dollars; acqui-hire IP deal.
demand_pricing: Win rates on large new deals above 35%, which management attributes partly to aiRA.
Existing-customer NRR of 111% split roughly: 4-5% from price escalators and overages, ~10% from upsell and new cohorts, net of ~5% churn.
Management frames loyalty as a red ocean; about 90 loyalty companies have revenue of USD10-100 million and are the M&A pool.
Acquired agency-model businesses run at ~30% gross margin; moving them onto the platform lifts gross margin to 65-75%.
Management says fewer than 10% of loyalty revenue sits with software vendors versus agencies; named competitors include Epsilon, Merkle, Kobie and Salesforce.

qa_highlights.question: What share of SessionM clients have migrated and what is the FY27 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No SessionM migrations before end-2026/early 2027; the full base is expected to take 2-3 years. 3-4 of ~45 customers are being fast-tracked; margins will improve through server cost cuts (SessionM server costs are ~50% of revenue vs ~7-9% at Capillary).

qa_highlights.question: Organic vs inorganic growth split and FX effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 organic growth was 17%; FX contributed about 6%; the rest is SessionM's two months. Cash is about half USD and half INR, which gives a natural hedge with the US at ~60% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cyber-fraud loss covered by insurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the bank-account fraud at a subsidiary is insured, but the amount and timing of recovery are not yet clear. No customer or employee data was exposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic NRR breakdown and churn?
qa_highlights.answer: Price escalators and overage are 4-5% of NRR; upsell and new cohorts add ~10%; churn is ~5%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aiRA figures net of cannibalisation and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ARR is ~USD2.5 million with no cannibalisation so far; gross and contribution margins are above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the SessionM purchase price INR17 crore when the deal was USD20 million?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD20 million enterprise value was adjusted for net debt at closing; the final true-up on April 30 brought the value to about INR17 crore; the entities are debt-free.

risks_watch: Q1 organic NRR excluding the healthcare account was 116%, but reported 111%; one large healthcare customer did not grow, which weighs on the quarter.
Enterprise budget cycles and ~9-month average deal cycles make quarterly new ACV lumpy (trailing-12-month metric).
Kognitiv migration milestone on September 1, 2026 is the first test of the AI-led upgrade approach; success is needed for the INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift.
Reported PAT is negative; the insurance recovery on the fraud loss is still uncertain.
aiRA is early: under 10 of ~26 live customers are paying, and the 5-10% revenue target depends on enterprise budget timing.
key_quotes: We will definitely beat our INR1,065 crores and revenue and INR172 crores number. I don't think we want to revise any guidance right now.
So, we will not start any SessionM migrations till probably end of this year, early next year, right.
Yes, so we are right now, I would say at like $2 million, $2.5 million in terms of revenue run rates on aiRA.
So, it's a it is going to be a big driver on the NRR side going forward as well.
But how much and when it would be recovered, I think that we don't have clarity on, so that work is in progress at this point in time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, AI product adoption and the SessionM and Kognitiv integration plans, and firm on keeping FY27 guidance unchanged while expecting to beat it. Management was more cautious on timing: SessionM migrations are not expected before end-2026, insurance recovery of the cyber-fraud loss is unclear, and the Q1 organic growth was partly weighed by one large healthcare customer.

adds.what: Kognitiv AI-led migration tool: first customer migration go-live (~16-17 customers total, full base by Sept 2027)
SessionM customer migration onto Capillary platform (3-4 of ~45 customers fast-tracked; full migration starts end-2026/early 2027)

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,065 crore and expects to beat it, with ~17% organic growth (about 20-23% including FX and acquisitions), ARR up 34% YoY to INR1,026 crore and new ACV expected up 30-40%; but no physical capacity or capex is being added, and growth is mainly acquisition- and software-driven.
